description:
## Outcome

One platform boundary resolves the per-user Jido state root and creates private state directories outside the installed release. `JIDO_HOME` replaces the default for tests and managed installations.

## Why now

The daemon, discovery record, token, logs, and durable sessions need a stable writable location. The package directory can be read-only and can change during an upgrade.

## Work

1. Add injected platform and environment resolution for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
2. Use `~/Library/Application Support/Jido` on macOS, `$XDG_STATE_HOME/jido` or `~/.local/state/jido` on Linux, and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Jido` on Windows.
3. Give `JIDO_HOME` full precedence when it is a valid absolute path.
4. Define named subdirectories for daemon runtime state, durable data, logs, and release cache.
5. Create directories with current-user access. Put Unix mode changes and Windows access control behind one capability boundary.
6. Normalize errors through `Jido.Cli.Error` at the CLI boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each platform default and precedence rule has a deterministic test.
- [ ] Paths with spaces and non-ASCII characters work.
- [ ] Relative, empty, or unsafe overrides fail with a configuration error and exit 64.
- [ ] State is never written inside the installed release directory.
- [ ] Directory creation does not broaden current-user access.
- [ ] Pure path resolution does not mutate the file system.

## Tests

Add state-root tests with injected environment, platform, home, and file-system functions. Run `mix quality`, `mix test --cover`, and `mix docs`.

## Non-goals

Do not store authentication tokens or discovery records in this task. Do not add system-wide state.
title: Resolve secure per-user state roots on every platform
